chunks: O differing minds and divided hearts,
whose bodies are present but wits are absent.
I am leading you (amicably) towards truthfulness, but you run away from it like goats running away from the howling of a lion!
How hard it is for me to uncover for you the secrets of justice, or to straighten the curve of truthfulness.
ai.seo_question: What is the meaning of Imam Ali's address to the people of Kufa regarding their differing minds and absent wits?
ai.summary: In this famous passage from Nahj al-Balagha, Imam Ali (peace be upon him) diagnoses the spiritual apathy of the Kufans, noting that their bodies were present but their minds and hearts were absent, leading to a 'flight from truth' comparable to goats fleeing a lion's roar. This critique highlights the core Shia scholarly theme that political legitimacy requires not just physical allegiance but intellectual and spiritual readiness, explaining why he initially hesitated to accept the caliphate amidst their inconsistency. The metaphor underscores the difficulty of establishing divine justice when the populace is intellectually detached from the reality of truth.

en.sayed-ali-raza: O (people of) differing minds and divided hearts,
whose bodies are present but wits are absent.
I am leading you (amicably) towards truthfulness, but you run away from it like goats and sheep running away from the howling of a lion.
How hard it is for me to uncover for you the secrets of justice, or to straighten the curve of truthfulness.
